previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of chronic pancreatitis, possibly due to sphincter of Oddi dysfunction, was admitted with several days of worsening abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting consistent with acute on chronic pancreatitis. She had not responded well to her usual nitroglycerin therapy. She was managed with NPO status, IV fluids, and IV Dilaudid for pain, with Reglan for nausea. Over the course of the admission, her symptoms improved, and she transitioned to oral pain medication and a regular diet. Imaging showed conflicting results: MRCP suggested chronic pancreatitis with ductal changes, while EUS was normal. A sphincterotomy was not performed due to risks, and the patient was referred for a second opinion with an outside gastroenterologist. She was discharged home with instructions to resume her prior medications, maintain a low-fat diet, and follow up closely.

radiology_notes.text:
MRCP

INDICATION:  Abdominal pain.

___.

TECHNIQUE:  Multiplanar T1- and T2-weighted imaging were acquired on a 1.5
Tesla magnet including dynamic 3D imaging obtained prior to, during and after
the uneventful intravenous administration of 15 mL of Magnevist.  In addition,
12 mcg of secretin was administered intravenously.  300 cc of GastroMARK and
450 cc of Redicat were administered orally.

FINDINGS: 

There is normal hepatic parenchymal signal intensity.  No focal liver lesion.
No intra- or extra-hepatic biliary dilatation.  There is conventional hepatic
arterial anatomy.  Visualized portal veins are patent.  

The pancreas has homogeneous signal intensity and enhances uniformly.  Main
pancreatic duct measures 2 mm at the head of the pancreas and 1.5 mm distally
pre administration of IV secretin.  Post secretin administration, there is
physiological dilatation of the pancreatic duct measuring 4 mm in the head and
2 mm in the body and tail.  There is no side branch dilatation appreciated on
today's study.  There is a paucity of fluid excretion into the duodenum
suggesting decreased fluid production / excretion and was previously described
also on prior studies.  There is no secondary evidence to suggest sphincter of
Oddi dysfunction or ampullary stenosis.  There is no sequela within the
pancreas to suggest chronic pancreatitis.  The pancreas has a relatively
homogeneous signal intensity and enhances uniformly.  Overall findings are
similar to prior imaging studies from ___.  

Both adrenal glands and kidneys are unremarkable.  There are no
retroperitoneal masses or adenopathy.  No abnormally dilated thickened small
or large bowel loop in the visualized abdomen.  No free fluid.  

Bone marrow signal is normal and there are no osseous lesions.

IMPRESSION:  

1.  Unremarkable signal intensity to pancreas with no sequelae of chronic
pancreatitis identified.  

2.  Normal physiological dilatation of the pancreatic duct with no side
branches apparent on today's examination.  There is no secondary evidence to
suggest sphincter of Oddi dysfunction or ampullary stenosis based on today's
imaging study. 

3.  Decreased fluid production and excretion of fluid into the duodenum post
secretin administration.  This is similar in volume when compared to prior
imaging study from ___.
